Subject: Production timeouts + 5xx/429 surge (urgent)

Sean —

We're seeing a huge increase in 5xx and 429 errors from the Redwood API starting ~08:45 PDT. Our production write path (daily claims ingestion) started returning timeouts; downstream systems are retrying and we're seeing a backlog. Example: ~30% error rate and multiple request IDs in the logs. This is impacting our live patient scoring pipeline — we had to pause the release.

I attached a small sample of failing request IDs and a snippet of the error stream. Can you confirm whether this is related to your Dedicated pool capacity or something on our side? We need an ETA on mitigation — our SRE is standing by.

Very concerned — this is live traffic for Lumina Health.

Vera Morris

Sean / Aditya — forwarding Lumina's report. Initial read from infra: Dedicated pool 'dedicated-us-west-2-5' shows sustained GPU utilization at >95% for last 40 minutes and autoscaler latencies spiking; eviction/rebalance events caused node readiness delay.

Immediate asks:
- Aditya: Can you validate whether the autoscaler failed to inject warm nodes and whether we had any blocked kubernetes pods due to preemption?
- If confirmed, please apply an emergency scale-up and consider a temporary override of the evaluation window (reduce to 30s) for the next 60 minutes.
- Sean: start routing 10–15% of Lumina traffic to hosted fallback and reduce concurrency on the largest model to lower per-request GPU time.

I'm attaching the capacity snapshot we've pulled. Will standby for logs.

- rdw-capacity-snapshot-20280325.csv

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production timeouts + 5xx/429 surge (urgent)

Marissa — confirmed. Observations from infra:
- Pool dedicated-us-west-2-5 hit GPU memory pressure; continuous batching queues lengthened which increased tail latency and produced 5xx responses when KV cache misses coincided.
- Autoscaler did attempt scale-up but the control loop's cooldown + our eviction threshold (0.85) prevented immediate node attachment; the scheduler then queued pods waiting for capacity.

Actions taken (10:00–10:10):
- Pushed two warm nodes to the pool and temporarily lowered the eviction threshold to 0.7.
- Applied an aggressive scale-up override for 30 minutes (will auto-revert at 10:40 PDT).
- Enabled routing rule: 12% of requests to Lumina now hit hosted fallback model variant (latency-optimized).

Preliminary metrics: errors down ~80% in the 10:05–10:10 window, tail latency reduced from 1.8s -> 0.7s for fallback traffic. Logging attached for sample request IDs.

I'll keep monitoring and will open an RCA ticket to dig into why the autoscaler cooldown didn't respond faster.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: Lumina Health incident — mitigation applied

Vera — quick update: we applied emergency mitigations at ~10:00 PDT (warm nodes + temporary scaling override + 12% hosted fallback routing). Early telemetry shows a significant drop in 5xx/429 and tail timeouts. Attached is the P0 dashboard screenshot for your team.

Next steps:
- We will keep the override for 60 minutes and then revert to normal autoscaler policy with a staged rollback.
- Eng (Aditya) is doing a deeper RCA; we expect a write-up within 48 hours.
- If you want a dedicated postmortem meeting, we can schedule a channel briefing with your SREs + our infra leads.

Can you confirm whether your side still sees errors in the last hour? If there are particular request IDs that still fail, please send them.

Thanks again for your patience — we know this is high impact.

Sean Gallagher
